text: created a script to use mouse+keyboard as xbox controller to play as player 2, i already had one xbox controller and i wanted to play with keyboard
Replaced the Typewriter component with a decode-style TextScramble. Characters resolve left to right through random chars. Feels like the terminal is thinking, not just typing.
The scramble-on-generate effect solved the dead zone between prompt submit and API response. Without it, the hero text just sat there for 2 seconds looking broken.
Moved briefing cache from in-memory Map to Redis. The Map worked fine in dev but serverless functions don't share memory across invocations. Every cold start was a cache miss.
Scrapped the trailing cursor shadow. Looked clever in isolation but felt like lag in practice. Subtlety beats gimmick every time.

I was building a job-hunt automation system. Part of it needed to post to X automatically.

Found xurl — looked clean, CLI-based, exactly what I wanted. Set it up. Ran it.

It died at the OAuth2 step every single time.

Spent way too long on it. Checked tokens, re-read docs, looked for env variables I might've missed. Nothing. Then found a GitHub issue — headless OAuth2 is a known bug. The CLI literally expects a browser to open and complete the redirect. In a headless session, that redirect never arrives. It just hangs.

I had two paths: shim a full Playwright browser session around a CLI tool just to do auth, or use the actual X API directly.

I chose the API. Should've started there.

The real thing I'm still thinking about — how much time do you give a tool before you call it? I kept assuming I was the problem. ◝(ᵔᗜᵔ)◜

What's your threshold before you swap tools?
